nc_snake_s_den.blurb: A small slab crag in national forest above Barnardsville, about half an hour from Asheville by car. Nearly all of the ten climbs are traditional leads, with one easy toprope, and the grades run from fifth-class scrambling through the 5.5 to 5.9 range. The cliff stands only a few steps from the dirt road, so there is almost no walk-in. It faces south and soaks up the sun in summer, so early or late in the day suits warm months, though the base itself is well shaded. The rock is modest in quality and the crowds are thin. The short, easy lines on the left side work for beginners, kids and anchor or rappel practice, but it is more a training spot than a destination.

nc_lower_tier_3.blurb: The Lower Tier of Section 3 sits in a former quarry at Rocky Face, a county park in Alexander County near Hiddenite. All ten routes here are top-ropes, mostly between 5.4 and 5.5, with the easiest at 5.2 and the hardest around 5.7. That makes it one of the gentlest spots in the park and a good choice for first-timers and kids. A short, rock-lined dirt path off the paved trail leads to the left end of the wall, where a third-class scramble gets you up to build anchors easily. The quarry face is sunny, and loose rock can fall now and then, so helmets are wise for climbers and belayers.

nc_lower_tier_2.blurb: The Lower Tier of Section 5 is a bolted wall in the old quarry at Rocky Face, near Hiddenite in Alexander County. Ten routes, mostly sport with a pair of trad lines, cover the 5.8 to 5.12 range, with the weight of them from 5.9 to 5.11. It suits climbers who have moved past the beginner walls in other sections and want steady, moderate-to-hard face pitches. The quarry face is sunny, and the rock quality varies, with loose pieces coming off from time to time, so wear a helmet when climbing or belaying.

nc_cougar_crag_the.blurb: A steep cliff at the far left end of the Dark Side, the north-facing cliff line in the Hickory Nut Gorge area, which sits across from Rumbling Bald. About ten climbs, nearly all traditional, with a single aid line. Grades range from 5.5 up to 5.12, but most of the free routes cluster in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it is mainly for experienced leaders comfortable on bold, overhanging lines. The wall is known for its steepness. The way in is involved: a trail past the Main Wall, a steep gully, a low-angle pitch, and a passage through a cave to reach the upper wall.
